scenes.narration: When most people hear the phrase "strategic networking," they jump straight to tactics.

vars.title: Who Will Walk This Next Chapter with You

scenes.narration: Who should I email? What should I say? How do I ask for help without being awkward? Those are important questions. But they're not the first ones.

vars.label: First instinct
vars.heading: Who, What, How
vars.chips: Who should I email?,What should I say?,How do I ask for help?

scenes.narration: Before you move into outreach and visibility, it's worth slowing down to ask a deeper one: who do I actually want walking alongside me in this next chapter, and why?

vars.statement: Who Do I Want Walking Alongside Me?
vars.iconCue: worth slowing down to ask a deeper one
vars.sub: In this next chapter, and why.

scenes.narration: This activity isn't just about making a list of names. It's about deliberately designing a small constellation of relationships that could matter for your future, not just your inbox this week.

pointCues: just about making a list of names

vars.statement: Design a Small Constellation of Relationships
vars.lines: Not just names on a list|Something that matters for your future

scenes.narration: As you think about your next move, whether that's a role transition, a new project, a shift in direction, or simply becoming more visible in your current work, certain people will matter more than others.

vars.label: Whatever the move
vars.heading: What Your Next Move Might Look Like

scenes.narration: Some people already understand parts of your story. They've seen you work. They know your strengths.
Others can help you see new possibilities: fields you haven't considered, roles you didn't know existed, paths that look different from what you see day to day.

vars.label: People who broaden the view
vars.heading: Others Help You See New Possibilities

scenes.narration: And some sit close to the actual opportunities you care about: decisions about roles, projects, budgets, hiring, or internal moves.

vars.heading: Some Sit Close to the Opportunities
vars.chips: Decisions about roles,Projects and budgets,Hiring or internal moves

scenes.narration: So in this reflection, you'll identify three to five specific people who could play important roles in your next chapter. You're going to look at each person through a few lenses.

vars.statement: Identify Three to Five Key People
vars.lines: Who could play a role in your next chapter|You'll look at each through a few lenses
vars.iconCue: important roles in your next chapter

scenes.narration: Who are they, and where do they sit in relation to your current or target field? What type of relationship do they represent?
A peer who walks alongside you, a sponsor who advocates for you, an opportunity holder who shapes roles and projects, or a mentor who helps you think clearly?

stepCues: a peer who walks alongside you
a sponsor who advocates for you
an opportunity holder who shapes roles
a mentor who helps you think clearly

scenes.narration: Why do they matter for your Next Move Statement or your future direction? And what would moving this relationship forward look like in the next 90 days?

vars.statement: Why They Matter, and What Comes Next
vars.lines: For your Next Move Statement, or future direction|Within the next 90 days
vars.iconCue: what would moving this relationship forward

scenes.narration: Instead of treating networking as a numbers game, talk to as many people as possible, you're treating it as a values and direction game.

pointCues: talk to as many people as possible

vars.aSub: Talk to as many people as possible

scenes.narration: Who genuinely fits into the story I'm building about my career? What kind of relationship would be meaningful and realistic with each person?

You'll write about why each person is relevant to your Next Move Statement. That might include what they see that you don't yet, what opportunities they're close to, or what kind of perspective or support they could offer.

chipCues: what they see that you don't yet

vars.label: What to capture
vars.heading: What You Might Be Missing
vars.chips: What they see,Opportunities they're close to,Perspective or support

scenes.narration: Then you'll define one specific, respectful outcome you'd like to aim for within the next 90 days. Things like having one

20-minute conversation about your next move, sharing your updated profile or resume and asking for feedback, exploring internal opportunities on their team, or asking for an introduction to someone in your target field.
At the end, you'll step back and look at the patterns in your list. Are most of your relationships inside your current organization?

vars.statement: Step Back and Look at Your List
vars.sub: Are most of your relationships inside your current organization?

scenes.narration: Do you have a mix of peers, sponsors, and opportunity holders, or is everything weighted toward one type? Which single relationship feels most important to nurture first, and why?

pointCues: a mix of peers, sponsors, and opportunity holders

vars.label: Look for patterns
vars.heading: Check the Balance of Your List
vars.point1: A mix of peers, sponsors, and opportunity holders?

scenes.narration: These answers matter, because they guide where you put your energy when you start taking action.

vars.statement: That Is Why These Answers Matter
